answer.rationale: P99 latency spike began 90 minutes ago, 2 hours post-release; this temporal correlation with the release is the strongest single signal in the current situation. Memory b1 shows rollback cleared a checkout error spike with the prior build stable and no customer impact. Memory b6 demonstrates staged gating works but a rollback remains the fastest path to restore baseline latency when a release is suspect and writes are at peak. Memory b2 is critical to review because it establishes that regional failover during heavy writes risks replication gaps and lost transactions—this eliminates failover as viable here despite its historical speed. Add_capacity requires provisioning time we don't have; route_read_replicas helps dashboard load (memory b5) but won't address write-path p99. Circuit breaker protects downstream but doesn't resolve the root latency cause. A small guarded rollback (canary-style, as in b6) on this suspected release limits blast radius while testing recovery before full rollback, minimizing risk to settlement traffic integrity.
